When syncing bundled DB records that have a UNIQUE index (e.g., agent_definitions with idx_agent_defs_name_scope_project), do NOT use import-then-delete to achieve atomicity — the import will fail with UNIQUE constraint violation because the old record still exists. Instead, use manager.update() for in-place atomic updates, which issues a single UPDATE SQL statement that can't leave the DB in an inconsistent state. The delete-then-import pattern is also risky because if import fails after delete, the old record is permanently lost. The manager.update() approach solves both problems.

Merging duplicate gwiki entity concept pages durably: union the loser's title+aliases into the survivor's frontmatter aliases, then delete the loser. This is stable because entity pages only re-synthesize from BROKEN-link clusters (upkeep derives its work queue from lint broken_links) — once [[Entity]] mentions resolve via the survivor's aliases, nothing recreates the deleted page. Entity-name wikilinks retarget automatically via aliases (page_targets resolution is case-insensitive over path/stem/title/aliases); path-form links like [[knowledge/sources/x]] must be retargeted by hand. Also: an alias exactly equal to the page title is pure redundancy (title is already a resolution key) and trips the duplicate_aliases lint. Applied in #17630: gobby-core→gcore, mcp-server→mcp, worker-process-spawning→spawn-agent merges with zero broken-link regressions (147→147, dup aliases 5→0).

Don't save memories for plans that haven't been implemented yet. Only save memories for things that are agnostic to the plan — general principles, user preferences, or factual discoveries about the codebase learned while investigating.

Why: In session #3368 (2026-04-22), after tabling a back-half pipeline plan, I saved a project memory describing design decisions from that unimplemented plan (integrator-as-persona, merge halt semantics). Josh rejected: 'I don't want to save memories of plans that haven't been implemented yet. If you learned something agnostic to the plan during your investigation, that's fine.' Unimplemented plans are speculative — they can be rewritten, abandoned, or superseded. Memorializing their design decisions poisons future sessions with 'we decided X' framings for decisions that were never committed to.

How to apply: After tabling or parking a plan, only save memory for content that survives the plan's deletion — durable design principles the user articulated (feedback), codebase facts discovered during research (reference), user preferences (user), or external-system pointers (reference). Do NOT save the plan's design decisions, phase structure, naming proposals, or architectural choices as project memories. When in doubt: would this memory still be useful if the plan were thrown out tomorrow? If no, skip it.

gwiki source pages have TWO naming schemes that must be reconciled by stable identity: (1) manifest-derived digest path `knowledge/sources/src-<id>.md` via `paths::derived_markdown_path(record)`, and (2) synthesis title-slug path `knowledge/sources/<slugify(title)>.md` via `synthesis::paths::source_page_paths`. A source id is `src-<16hex content_hash>-<location-slug>` (built by `sources::render::source_id(canonical_location, content_hash)`); the content hash ROTATES on every re-fetch while the location slug is STABLE. Any identity match/dedup/link-resolution MUST key on the stable location slug (everything after the hash), NOT the full hash-prefixed id — see `compile::select::source_id_slug` and (added #17705) `synthesis::paths::source_identity_slug`. `page_matches_source_identity` originally required an exact `source_path` frontmatter match, so hash rotation (and legacy stubs lacking that frontmatter key) minted `-2` sibling stubs and left sources uncompiled. This volatile-hash-identity disease is the shared root cause behind #17705 (duplicate stubs / stuck uncompiled), #17704 defect 2 (dangling concept->source links), and #17702 (topic-compile stale hash pointers).

FIXED for links in #17704 (commit on 0.5.0): `crates/gcore/src/vault/lint.rs::source_identity_lookup_key` emits a private-keyspace stable key (`\x01source-identity\x01knowledge/sources/<slug>`) for any `knowledge/sources/src-<hex>-<slug>` PAGE (in `page_targets`) AND LINK (in `link_lookup_keys`), so a link minted against an old hash still resolves to the page under its rotated name whenever they share the location slug. Shared gcore lint => covers `gwiki lint` + `gwiki trust`/health; on-disk, no re-index. Verified live 2026-07-07 gwiki 0.8.0: session-source danglers 19 -> 0 (sessions 3e4c4a13 rotated to src-103b0fac, ec749a42 to src-efd2ef44). Does NOT change the deliberate content-addressed naming.

The gobby web UI has a split styling approach: the chat UI (web/src/components/chat/) uses Tailwind CSS with its own styles.css importing tailwindcss plus additional non-Tailwind styles from the index.css decomposition. All other pages use component-scoped CSS files (e.g., SessionsPage.css, TerminalsPage.css, tasks-page.css) imported by their React components, with shared CSS custom properties (--font-size-base: 16px, --font-mono, --font-sans) and global styles in web/src/styles/index.css (703 lines). index.css was decomposed from 13,849 lines into 16 component-scoped files. When matching styles between chat and non-chat components, map Tailwind classes to their CSS equivalents (e.g., text-xs = 0.75rem, py-1.5 = 0.375rem, px-4 = 1rem).

For sandbox-tolerant hooks rev1 local testing, the Rust ghook binary is already built and present at ~/.gobby/bin/ghook, but it has not been published to GitHub Releases or crates.io yet. Phase 2 Rust-side tasks are already closed; Python-side work should assume a local ghook for testing before publish.

Migration tests that simulate a pre-migration DB state (e.g., test_migration_103.py setting schema_version=102) must also create tables that later migrations expect. Migration 107 alters agent_definitions (created by migration 92), so any test starting at v102 must include agent_definitions in its manual setup.

Bundled rules split from 11 group YAML files into ~80 individual files in group subdirectories under src/gobby/install/shared/rules/<group-name>/. Old group files moved to deprecated/. Individual files use tags: [group-name] instead of group: field. sync_bundled_rules() skips deprecated/ via path filter and has orphan cleanup for removed rules.

Task #17020 added the Rules activity tab under web/src/components/activity. The tab uses useRulesTabData plus focused rules subcomponents, reuses the shared activity panel list/detail patterns, adds dirty-guarded editing and serialized copy/save mutations via useRules, and registers the tab in ActivityPanelTabs/useActivityPanel/ActivityPanel. Validation for commit 062ffc92a: web type-check, focused Vitest RulesTab/useActivityPanel/ActivityPanel tests, JS/CSS/token linting, test-quality audit, git diff --check, and web build all passed. Chrome DevTools MCP verified dark/light mobile rendering at 390x844 with 44px controls, wrapped toolbar, filter dropdown inside viewport, no horizontal overflow, and accessible row/action controls.

Gobby #14938 moved dispatcher heartbeat candidate reload and context-building helpers from `src/gobby/dispatch/dispatcher.py` into `src/gobby/dispatch/context.py`. `dispatcher.py` keeps importing and re-exporting `build_context`, `reload_candidate`, and `_field` so existing tests and monkeypatch surfaces remain compatible while the file stays below the 1,000-line source limit.

Gobby #15336 fixed Claude isolated agent spawns: _spawn_claude_terminal now builds the Claude command without the prompt, adds --mcp-config <workspace>/.mcp.json and --strict-mcp-config when the workspace MCP config exists, applies sandbox args, then appends the prompt. This prevents conflicting user/project gobby MCP scopes from hiding Gobby verdict tools in spawned Claude QA agents.

Gobby test-quality analyzer skips functions decorated as pytest fixtures (`fixture`, `pytest.fixture`, `pytest_asyncio.fixture`) during test discovery, even when their names start with `test_`. Added in task #14272 commit c6dfeb381.

P2P Agent Infrastructure: AgentCommandManager lives in src/gobby/storage/agent_commands.py. It manages parent-child session commands with lifecycle: pending → running → completed/failed/cancelled. InterSessionMessageManager now has get_undelivered_messages() and mark_delivered() for delivery tracking. LocalSessionManager.is_ancestor() walks parent_session_id chain with cycle guard. Migration v116 added message_type, metadata_json, delivered_at columns to inter_session_messages and created agent_commands table.

Bug #9064: close_task in _lifecycle.py failed to clear task_claimed/claimed_task_id session variables after successful close. Root cause: the claimed_task_id comparison and clearing logic was outside the `if state:` block where claimed_task_id was defined, and the outer `except Exception: pass` silently swallowed any errors. Fix: moved comparison+clearing inside `if state:`, added UUID normalization for robust comparison, replaced silent exception swallowing with logger.warning(). File: src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle.py lines ~250-290. The observer fallback in observers.py intentionally does NOT clear for Claude Code (no tool_output in AFTER_TOOL hooks), so CC users are entirely dependent on this MCP proxy clearing code.

As of gobby-#17331, daemon codewiki refresh is shared through `CodewikiRefreshService` in `src/gobby/code_index/codewiki_refresh.py`. The post-commit `CodewikiRefreshTrigger` only gates/debounces `wiki.codewiki_on_commit` and logs best-effort failures; nightly cron registration lives in `src/gobby/code_index/codewiki_nightly.py`, creates/reconciles one disabled-by-default system job named `gobby:codewiki-nightly:<project_id>` with handler `codewiki_nightly:<project_id>`, schedules `0 3 * * *` in host-local/configured timezone, and stores cron execution timestamps as UTC via CronJobStorage. Default output remains `<repo>/gobby-wiki`, not `<repo>/codewiki`, to match the gwiki vault migration.

Gobby docs/runbooks/postgres-rollback.md is now a PostgreSQL recovery export runbook, not a SQLite runtime rollback runbook. It documents cutover-ticket parsing, pgaudit-managed/pgaudit-file/wal-archive/none capture_kind export paths, artifact attachment, and PostgreSQL fix-forward/operator-managed restore guidance. `gobby postgres deactivate` is removed and `hub_backend=sqlite` is not a supported runtime path.

Merge agent removed from autonomous dev-loop and orchestrator pipelines (commit c0508c2c). Merge is now manual — the pipeline terminates when all tasks reach review_approved status. The merge agent definition still exists but is not spawned by any pipeline. Reason: pushing to remote and closing tasks autonomously is the highest-risk operation and should be tested on a test project with packaged gobby before enabling. The merge agent also has a no-push conflict with worker-safety rules that needs resolution (push should be an MCP tool, not raw Bash).

Architectural direction in progress: Gobby is making Haiku/Sonnet no longer required for feature configs by opening LLM-backed feature configuration to all CLI/ACP adapters. New LLM-backed features should avoid hardcoded Anthropic model names and design against adapter-agnostic feature config/routing where possible.

Critical bug: If hook_dispatcher.py is deleted or missing while Claude Code hooks are configured, the Stop hook failure creates an infinite loop. Each response triggers the stop hook, which fails and generates a new 'Stop hook feedback' message, which triggers another response, ad infinitum. The only way to break the loop is for the user to Ctrl+C and fix the hook file externally. The agent cannot fix it because PreToolUse hooks also fail, blocking all tool calls. Root cause in this case was unclear — the file existed at ~/.gobby/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py but uv run couldn't find it temporarily (possibly during venv rebuild or daemon restart).

Context-window resolution is source-aware. Use gobby.llm.context_windows for precedence: explicit overrides, provider-reported runtime metadata, provider-reported/provider-owned catalog values, OpenRouter/model_costs registry, then static defaults. Provider model entries should carry context_length_source so stale source-less cache values do not outrank registry/runtime data.

DECISION (2026-04-23): For #12651 skill fetch directives, use the canonical wording `Call get_skill(name="<skill>") on gobby-skills, then continue.` Do not tell agents to pass `session_id` inside get_skill arguments; when Gobby invokes tools through the MCP proxy, session context belongs to the outer call/proxy context, not the inner tool args. Use `loaded_skills` as the replacement ledger for successful agent-visible skill fetches, not `injected_skills`.

gobby-cli now has pinned daemon-facing CLI contracts for gcode and gwiki. `gcode contract --format json` must match `crates/gcode/contract/gcode.contract.json`; `gwiki contract --format json` must match `crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json`. Contract-adjacent changes should update the JSON contract, `docs/contracts/*`, and contract drift tests together. `gcode codewiki` has command-level `--scope`; gwiki uses global `--project`/`--topic` and explicitly has no `--scope`. Gwiki AI routes are `auto|daemon|direct|off`, and `gwiki research` follows `docs/contracts/gwiki-research.md` rather than the old daemon agent-spawn shape.

The plugin system was removed per the workflows-v2 plan (docs/plans/workflows-v2.md). MCP tools replace plugins as the extension mechanism. However, the removal was incomplete — CLI commands (src/gobby/cli/extensions.py), ClaudePluginsProvider (src/gobby/skills/hubs/claude_plugins.py), and registrations in __init__.py and runner.py still exist. Task #9067 tracks the source removal.

Task #17326 removed SessionSource.GEMINI and added SessionSource.UNKNOWN plus parse_session_source() as the tolerant dynamic-source parser. Legacy persisted source='gemini' rows are relabeled by migration 295_relabel_gemini_sessions for sessions and session_stop_signals; storage read paths for tmux pane monitor, agent termination, session context, and chat lifecycle now use parse_session_source() so stale or future source values become UNKNOWN instead of raising ValueError.

In Gobby task stage-state transitions, RuntimeDispatchMutex holder is derived from by_session_id (or 'system'). Recovery code that needs to call stage_states.fail_stage under a dispatch mutex should acquire the mutex with holder 'recovery' and pass by_session_id='recovery'; fail_stage releases that mutex when its internal context exits, so recovery must reacquire before subsequent guarded writes such as release_task_claim.

In `TaskSyncManager.import_from_github_issues`, imported GitHub issues must be stored with a valid Gobby task_type such as `task`; `issue` is not in `VALID_TASK_TYPES` and causes `Task.from_row` hydration failures. LocalSessionManager (storage/sessions.py) uses get() not get_session() to fetch a single session by ID. The sessions/manager.py SessionManager has get_session() but the storage layer does not.

Claude aliases/canonical IDs, Qwen auth suffixes, and Droid Core provider prefixes remain supported.

Isolated gwiki smoke-test vault recipe: gwiki project scope requires a project identity file, so to test the installed ~/.gobby/bin/gwiki against a throwaway vault, create <dir>/.gobby/project.json with just {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<name>"}, then run `gwiki init --project <dir>` (creates <dir>/wiki), and use `gwiki <cmd> --project <dir>` for ingest-file/sources/refresh/upkeep/lint etc. Use --no-ai on ingest-file to avoid AI routing — note --no-ai ingest writes ONLY the raw capture (raw/<src-id>.md) and manifest entry; it does NOT create the derived digest, so hand-seed wiki/knowledge/sources/<src-id>.md yourself for digest-dependent smoke tests (upkeep clustering, supersede/refresh cleanup). Source-manifest details for smoke assertions: the manifest is NOT a JSON file — it is `<!-- gwiki-source {json} -->` marker lines in wiki/raw/INDEX.md (SourceManifest::read/index_path); record ids are the raw filename stems (raw/<src-id>.md), and `gwiki refresh` takes repeatable `--id <src-id>` flags. Discovered while fixing #17650/#17651/#17652; useful for #17653 and any future gwiki ingest work.

Gobby dispatch mutexes attached to active agent runs must be refreshed during normal AgentLifecycleMonitor maintenance, not only daemon restart recovery. Use TaskDispatchMutexManager.refresh_mutex_for_run(task_id, run_id, ttl_seconds) so only existing matching active-run mutex rows are extended; do not mask active_run_expired_lease in observability or create new mutex rows for manual agents.

As of 2026-06-28, Gobby's SecretStore derives its Fernet key from the local machine_id plus a shared salt, and SecretStore.get returns None on InvalidToken. In a shared PostgreSQL hub / remote daemon setup, client-side config loading that resolves $secret values may fail to decrypt secrets created on the daemon machine unless the design routes secret resolution through the daemon or changes the identity model.

For gobby-cli task #557 / gwiki shared-code Falkor edge limits, the accepted configuration surface is config_store plus ~/.gobby/gcore.yaml only; do not add .env or GOBBY_* environment-variable overrides for these gwiki edge-limit settings.

Current Gobby build automation behavior: explicit `gobby build ...` ticks respect the project dispatcher hard stop. If `gobby:dispatcher.enabled=false` from `gobby build stop`, build kick helpers return `dispatcher_cron_disabled` until `gobby build resume` re-enables the row. Idle parking uses enabled=true with next_run_at=NULL and can be woken by build/startup paths.

Upstream ghook distribution mapping for block-observability work: the installed `ghook` binary is published on crates.io as crate `gobby-hooks`, and crates.io points it to `https://github.com/GobbyAI/gobby-cli` with source under `crates/ghook`. Gobby FalkorDB Docker installer contract: installer module `src/gobby/cli/installers/falkor.py` resolves passwords as provided > existing `databases.falkordb.requirepass` secret > generated, validates with `validate_falkordb_password`, writes config_store and `bootstrap.yaml` only after Docker health returns PONG, stores bootstrap key `falkordb_password`, maps Redis to host port 16379 and browser to 13000, and returns `password_source` plus `password` only for generated values.

Agent run stale-timeout cleanup now keys off child session heartbeat (`sessions.updated_at`) before timing out long-running runs, and timeout persistence backfills `tool_calls_count` and `turns_used` from linked session stats so active work is not mislabeled as a zero-activity timeout.

Pipeline CLI approval commands (`gobby pipelines approve` and `gobby pipelines reject`) should prefer the daemon HTTP routes (`/api/pipelines/approve/{token}` and `/api/pipelines/reject/{token}`) so daemon-started pipeline resumes keep the daemon's MCP/LLM-capable execution environment. Local executor fallback is only for unreachable or unhealthy daemon cases.

Root cause of the 'vision_status: extracted with empty text' symptom: gemma-4-*-qat is a REASONING model that emits hidden reasoning_content first. With a small max_tokens (e.g. 300) it spends the whole budget reasoning and emits 0 visible content tokens (empty). ## gcode Agent Usage Regression Investigation

**Regression:** Agents have shifted from using `gcode` almost exclusively to almost completely ignoring it, despite existing rules enforcing code-index usage.

**Root Cause Hypothesis:**
Instruction precedence and hook timing. Global Codex instructions (which say "use rg first for file/text search") load earlier in the context window than Gobby's project-specific enforcement. The current `require-code-index` hook is reactive (loads the skill *after* an agent violates it) rather than preventive (blocks broad rg upfront).

**Why This Matters:**
Once an agent uses rg successfully, it stays in context and becomes the path of least resistance. The local code-index skill can't compete with a stronger always-present habit unless enforcement makes gcode the path of least resistance.

**Recommended Fixes:**
1. Add PreToolUse hook to block broad rg/grep/find/sed over source/test trees when code-index is available. Allow narrow follow-up reads (e.g., `sed -n '120,150p'`) only after a recent gcode call.
2. Track per-turn search ratio (gcode calls vs shell search/read). Warn when broad shell search happens before gcode.
3. Improve hook message: instead of just "load code-index," say: "Use gcode search-content/search-symbol/outline first. Use rg/sed only for exact narrow follow-up after gcode locates the file/line."
4. Consider a `gcode grep` compatibility command for agents reaching for rg syntax from muscle memory.

**Status:** Investigation underway. Session #6347 has concrete examples of agents ignoring gcode.

**Related:** [[tool-usage-preference]] discusses preference for gcode over sed/rg for token efficiency.

Codex native plan-approval capture findings + procedural gotchas (Path B task #15728, epic #15647; see capture procedure memory 59385f3f). Codex CLI v0.138.0. RESULT: codex has a native Plan mode (`/plan`, config key plan_mode_reasoning_effort). When the model proposes a plan it renders ONE approval menu (single shape): 'Implement this plan?  1. Yes, implement this plan (Switch to Default and start coding)  2. Yes, clear context and implement (Fresh thread)  3. No, stay in Plan mode (Continue planning)  / Press enter to confirm or esc to go back'. The item NUMBER selects AND activates immediately (verified: pressing '3' alone fired with no Enter; 'Press enter to confirm' is only for arrow-key nav). Codex's plan menu has a SINGLE approve semantic (no auto/bypass-vs-manual choice; post-plan approval mode comes from --ask-for-approval, not this menu), so plan_options approve_yolo AND approve_act both map to digit '1', request_changes maps to '3'. Single shape => static registry.register (no pane-aware resolver), so requires_pane('codex') is False. Registered in src/gobby/adapters/plan_keystrokes.py _CODEX_PLAN_MENU. PROCEDURAL GOTCHAS for capturing codex's native menu: (1) gobby installs codex hooks (~/.codex/config.toml [features] hooks=true) incl. a PermissionRequest hook that auto-handles/auto-approves command approvals, SUPPRESSING the native TUI approval menu — launch with `--disable hooks` to see the raw native menu. (2) macOS read-only sandbox still permits writes to /tmp (TMPDIR); to force a command-approval escalation target a write OUTSIDE the sandbox (e.g. $HOME) — but for PLAN approval just use `/plan` + a planning task, no escalation needed. (3) ChatGPT-account auth REJECTS `-m gpt-5-codex` ('not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account'); omit -m to use the account default (gpt-5.5). (4) launching codex inside the gobby repo pulls in the full UserPromptSubmit skill-loading injection which makes codex deliberate/burn quota — capture in a throwaff /tmp dir for speed (the native menu shape is cwd-independent). Same tmux survival trick as 59385f3f: start the server with `-f /dev/null` (or set destroy-unattached off) since the user's ~/.tmux.conf sets destroy-unattached on globally. Secondary menu (per-command approval, NOT used for plan approval): '1. Yes, proceed (y) / 2. Yes, and don't ask again (p) / 3. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)'.

Stdio MCP child process stderr is routed by passing MCPClientManager(stdio_errlog_path=...) through create_transport_connection(..., stdio_errlog_path=...) into StdioTransportConnection, which opens that path and passes it as errlog to mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client. The daemon runner supplies runner.config.telemetry.log_file_mcp_client so raw child diagnostics go to the MCP client log instead of daemon stderr; managers without a path explicitly fall back to sys.stderr.

Clone `use_local: true` clones from committed HEAD, not the working tree. Uncommitted deletions (shown as ` D` in git status) will still be present in the clone. Always commit cleanup before cloning if you want a clean state.
agents.md is a reserved filename for Codex CLI. Don't use it for gobby documentation. The agent definitions guide should be at docs/guides/agent_definitions.md instead.

gobby-local (gloc) is a local LLM launcher crate at crates/gloc/. Auto-detects LM Studio and Ollama backends, manages Ollama model lifecycle (check/pull/warmup), sets env vars from YAML config templates, and exec()s into AI CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex). Config follows gsqz layered pattern: built-in default → ~/.gobby/gloc.yaml → .gobby/gloc.yaml → --config. Backends are an ordered Vec (probe order matters), clients are a BTreeMap with template env vars ({backend.url}, {backend.auth_token}, {model}). Implemented in session #27, committed 2026-04-07.

Gobby build lifecycle contract: plan-file builds default to planning -> expansion -> development -> holistic_qa -> pr -> merge; --skip-stage pr removes only pr, yielding planning -> expansion -> development -> holistic_qa -> merge. Per-stage cap overrides such as --stage planning:max_work_attempts=99,max_review_rounds=99 are cap-only and must not narrow the lifecycle. Planning and plan-adversary work should run without workspace isolation even when development-forward stages use worktree or clone isolation.

Repeatable recipe for the epic #445 monolith-split tasks (#446-#459: split a >1000-line Rust source file into a directory of <1000-line modules, preserving public API and behavior). COMPLETE: all 14 leaf tasks landed on `dev`. Worked cleanly on codewiki.rs (2,586 -> 10 files), video.rs (1,734 -> 5 files), provisioning.rs (1,721 -> 5 files), research.rs (1,678 -> 6 files), config.rs (1,488 -> 4 files), commands/refresh.rs (1,243 -> 7 files), ingest/document.rs (1,213 -> 5 files), compile.rs (1,214 -> 5 files), gcode db.rs (1,054 -> 3 files: mod facade w/ pub-use re-export globs + resolution + queries), gcode import_resolution/parser.rs (1,045 -> 6 files: facade dispatcher + 5 per-language children — see gotcha (p)), sources.rs (1,019 -> 6, gotcha q), ingest/pdf.rs (1,041 -> 6, gotchas q/r), and research_loop.rs (1,090 -> 5: facade + types/engine/helpers/tests — see gotcha (s)). INTEGRATION-TEST CRATE (#454): tests/cli_smoke.rs (1,176 -> 4 files) used a DIFFERENT pattern — see gotcha (o). Steps: (1) `gcode outline <file>` to map symbols, but BEWARE gcode outline FLATTENS nested `mod` blocks and does NOT show containment — grep column-0 braces `grep -nE '^\}' file` and column-0 item starts `grep -nE '^[a-zA-Z#]' file` to find real module/type boundaries (e.g. codewiki had an inline `mod prompts {}` that the outline hid; config.rs has nested `pub mod embedding_keys`/`pub mod ai_keys` the outline flattened — derive their end lines by brace-depth). Also `gcode grep 'derive|cfg\(|impl |pub struct|pub enum' <file>` to map attribute lines + impl/struct/enum starts in one shot. (2) Identify the external API: `gcode grep '<name>::' | grep -v <file>` — note EVERY externally-referenced pub symbol so the facade re-exports them as `pub` (not pub(crate)). BETTER (used #451): write a small uv-python script that, for each top-level symbol, records which line-range SEGMENT each reference falls in — anything referenced in >1 production segment is cross-module and must be widened; everything else stays private. This computes the EXACT minimal widening set up front instead of reacting to compiler errors. #456 EXTENDED this: also run the script over the IMPORTED names (the original `use` block) per-segment to compute LEAN per-child import sets exactly (every helper/predicate/context/models name assigned to the child(ren) whose body text contains it; verify the union == the original import block so nothing is orphaned or double-counted). #459 RE-CONFIRMED: also run the script over the test body separately to compute the explicit imports the moved tests.rs needs (gotcha n). TOOLING CAVEAT (#453): `gcode grep` does NOT support `\b`/word-boundary (a `\b...\b` pattern silently returns ZERO rows, indistinguishable from 'no refs') and matches SUBSTRINGS, so symbol-ref sweeps are noisy — filter to the target file with `grep -E '^[0-9]+:'` and verify each ref line against the segment boundaries; for exact field/type cross-refs READ the orchestrator + struct bodies via `uv run --no-project python` pathlib (or `gcode symbol <uuid>`) rather than trusting grep counts. ALSO (#455): `gcode grep '<pat>' <dir>` (directory arg) can silently return NOTHING — it is unreliable for cross-file external-ref enumeration; prefer reading bodies + the re-export-glob facade approach which makes external-ref enumeration UNNECESSARY (see step 4 re-export variant). A gobby-cli task was filed (#471) to add word-boundary/whole-word support to gcode grep and error on unsupported regex. (3) Carve byte-verbatim line ranges into the new dir. PRIMARY METHOD NOW (#449/#450): the prefer-gcode hook was TIGHTENED and BLOCKS `sed -n` reads/redirects of source AND Read of any source file (even small ranges) — which ALSO means the Edit tool is unusable (it requires a prior Read), so ALL post-carve fixups must go through a `uv run --no-project python` script too (pathlib read + str.replace + write; hook-immune; bare python is blocked, `uv run` is not; `git show HEAD:<path> | uv run --no-project python` works to re-read an ALREADY-DELETED original). The carve splitter reads the file via pathlib and writes each child by 1-indexed inclusive line range. `gcode imports <file>` still gives the import block; `gcode grep` still works for boundary mapping. Skill gates ALSO fire on the first file write under a claimed task — load rust, python, context7, development-discipline, code-index via gobby-skills get_skill when prompted, then proceed (in #451-#456 the WRITE of the carve .py itself triggered the gate chain rust->development-discipline->python->context7 in sequence; each blocks the write until loaded, so load all four, then re-issue the identical Write; and close/create gates fire task-transitions + task-creation on first close_task/create_task schema fetch). NOTE (#459): writing the carve/analysis .py via `cat > /tmp/x.py << 'EOF'` HEREDOC (Bash) instead of the Write tool AVOIDS the skill-gate chain entirely (gates fire on the Write/Edit TOOL, not on shell file writes or uv-python pathlib writes) — the whole point of the python carve approach. A CLI `/compact` RESETS the per-session skill-gate state, so after a compaction the rust->development-discipline->python->context7 chain (and task-transitions on close) FIRES AGAIN on the next Write-tool write/close — just reload them. (4) Build a `mod.rs` FACADE holding: top imports, consts, the orchestration entrypoint(s), `mod x;` decls, re-exports, plus `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. RE-EXPORT-GLOB VARIANT (#455, BEST for a FLAT utility module that is just a bag of pub fns over a shared resource like a DB Client): do NOT hoist the pub API into the facade body — instead relocate cohesive groups WHOLESALE into children KEEPING their existing `pub` (no widening, no per-symbol analysis), and put `pub use child::*;` globs in mod.rs. Every pub name stays reachable at `crate::<mod>::NAME` regardless of which child owns it, so you do NOT need to enumerate external callers at all (private items can't be referenced externally anyway, so moving them is always safe). db.rs #455: mod.rs kept only the 3 connection primitives (connect_readwrite/connect_readonly/read_config_value, which need `postgres::Client` + `crate::schema`) + `mod queries; mod resolution; pub use queries::*; pub use resolution::*;`; resolution.rs got the whole DB-URL resolve chain + broker (ureq, fully-qualified) + consts + the 2 private structs + ALL the unit tests (every test was a resolution/broker test, so they move with resolution and see its privates via the test mod's own `use super::*;` — ZERO widening); queries.rs got GraphFileFacts + the graph/file/symbol query fns (all take `&mut impl GenericClient`). Both children are SELF-CONTAINED (no `use super::*;` at module level — gotcha (i)). DISPATCHER-IN-FACADE VARIANT (#456): keep the dispatcher entrypoint(s) in the facade calling private per-segment fns now in children; widen ONLY the facade-called fns to pub(crate); facade `use child::*;` (plain) globs make them resolve unqualified — see gotcha (p). DATA TYPE PLACEMENT (facade-body variant, #449-#453): keep a type in the parent facade ONLY if it is accessed cross-module via PRIVATE fields (descendants see ancestor privates, so parent-placement avoids widening). In #449 ALL public API types + `run` stayed in mod.rs; #450 split data-contracts(types.rs)/resolution(resolve.rs)/tests; #451 refresh by WORKFLOW STAGE (selection/candidate/vault/render/model DTOs as pub(crate)); #452 document by MODALITY (office/html/render); #453 compile by PIPELINE STAGE (collect/index/render) + CollectedSources pub(crate) struct w/ PRIVATE fields in mod root + index_lock_timeout kept at crate::compile root for external refs. CHILDREN see parent PRIVATE items via `use super::*;`, so parent->child needs NO widening; only child->sibling-child (through the pub-only re-export glob) needs widening. PARENT re-export: plain non-pub `use child::*;` AVOIDS the 'glob reexports nothing pub' warning and is enough when the facade/descendants consume names; use `pub use child::*;` when you must PRESERVE genuinely-pub API at the parent path (#455), and `pub(crate) use child::*;` / `pub(crate) use child::Name;` when the parent module is itself `pub(crate) mod` and consumers reference `crate::<mod>::Name` (#459: research_loop is `pub(crate) mod`, so facade used `pub(crate) use {engine::ResearchLoop, helpers::*, types::*}`). (5) Each child file: prepend `use super::*;` ONLY IF the child actually references a parent/sibling item (gotcha (i) — a self-contained child must OMIT it, e.g. #455 resolution.rs + queries.rs both omit it, #456 all 5 children omit it; #459 children import siblings via explicit `use super::{types,helpers,engine}::{..}` and OMIT the bare glob); the relocated `mod tests` body usually ALREADY starts with `use super::*;` inside it — do NOT double-prepend; add anonymous `as _` trait imports only to files that need them — the glob does NOT carry `as _` imports; widen module-level private fns/structs/enums/types called CROSS-MODULE via targeted str.replace (regex MULTILINE `^fn NAME`->`pub(crate) fn NAME`, NOT `fn NAME(` which misses generic/lifetime sigs) per-name from the cross-module set computed in step (2), OR (re-export variant) skip widening entirely by keeping items `pub` + `pub use child::*`. (6) GOTCHAS that cause errors/clippy -D warnings: (a) widening fns to pub(crate) while their param/return TYPES stay private -> `private_interfaces` warning -> bump those structs/enums to pub(crate) too; (b) a `pub fn` moved into a private submodule and re-exported via `pub(crate) use x::*` DOWNGRADES it from public -> use `pub use x::*`. CONVERSELY (#449): a child with NO pub items (only pub(crate) helpers) re-exported via `pub use child::*` triggers `warning: glob import doesn't reexport anything with visibility pub` (fails -D warnings) -> use `pub(crate) use child::*` for helper-only children, and `pub use child::*` ONLY for children that export genuinely-pub fns (#455 resolution+queries both have pub fns -> `pub use`). Decide per-child by grepping `^pub fn|^pub struct|^pub enum` in the child AFTER widening; (c) functions used ONLY by `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (incl. `#[cfg(test)] fn` helpers) must be pub(crate)+re-exported so a SIBLING tests.rs sees them via super::* — BUT if the whole test module moves INTO the same child as the code it tests (#455: all tests -> resolution.rs), they see privates directly via the test mod's `use super::*;` and NO widening is needed; (d) parent's own now-unused imports must be deleted (compiler is authoritative; add/remove reactively from build warnings); (e) CARVE BOUNDARY GOTCHA — START: `gcode outline` reports `line_start` at the keyword line, NOT at a preceding attribute. If a carved segment's FIRST item has an attribute above it (`#[derive(...)]`, `#[cfg(...)]`, `#[test]`, doc comment), a `line_start`-anchored carve silently DROPS it -> E0599/E0277/missing-test (#452 `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`; #453 `#[derive(...)]` above structs; #454 `#[test]` above each group's first fn — carve started at the attr line). END (#455, the MIRROR): a trailing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block's CLOSING `}` sits on the FILE's LAST line, BEYOND the last test fn's outline `line_end` (the fn's `line_end` is the INNER fn brace; the module brace is +1) — carving `seg(test_attr, last_fn_end)` DROPS the module's own closing brace -> rustc 'this file contains an unclosed delimiter'. Carve a trailing test module through the FILE's final line; VERIFY each carved child ends with a column-0 `}`. (f) cross-module STRUCT FIELD READ needs `pub(crate)` fields (E0616), cross-module INHERENT impl methods need `pub(crate)` (E0624) — but NEVER add a visibility modifier to a trait-impl method (compile error; #451 skipped `fn from(` of `impl From<...>`). (f2) E0451: when the PARENT facade CONSTRUCTS a child's struct via literal syntax OR DESTRUCTURES it, those struct FIELDS must each be `pub(crate)` too (distinct from E0616 reading). RULE for a split where one orchestrator fn touches nearly every type (refresh's execute): make the whole DTO module pub(crate) struct + pub(crate) fields wholesale via a line-by-line state machine (skip `#[serde(..)]`/attr lines + impl bodies). (g) MOVED-FILE RELATIVE PATHS: `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` resolve relative to the file holding the macro, so moving `src/foo.rs` -> `src/foo/mod.rs` (one dir deeper) breaks every relative asset path — add one `../`. (h) COHESION OVER WIDENING: when a candidate child's symbols are consumed by exactly ONE sibling, MERGE into that sibling instead of split+widen. Compiler is authoritative (E0425/E0422 name the missing fn/struct + its DEFINITION site as the 2nd `-->`). (i) (#450/#455/#456/#459): a SELF-CONTAINED child that references NOTHING from super (pure data/util module using only fully-qualified std::/anyhow:: paths + its own imports, e.g. config/types.rs, db/queries.rs, db/resolution.rs, parser/python_js.rs) MUST OMIT `use super::*;` — under -D warnings the glob trips `unused_imports`. Add `use super::*;` ONLY to children that actually use a parent/sibling item; prefer explicit `use super::{child}::{Name}` over the bare glob for sibling refs. (j) (#450): SELF-REFERENTIAL `include_str!("<orig>.rs")` inside CI-guard tests, AND any test that hardcodes the source path, break after the split: loop `include_str!` over each NEW production file, and repoint the allowed-path guard to the file that now owns the guarded literals. VERIFY via `RUN_SLOW_TESTS=1 cargo test -p <pkg> <scan_test>`. (k) (#450/#453): items imported by OTHER crate modules as `crate::<mod>::X` must stay reachable at that EXACT path — cleanest to keep such an item in the facade ROOT (mod.rs) OR use the `pub use child::*` re-export variant (#455) which preserves ALL pub names at `crate::<mod>::*` automatically; #459 used named `pub(crate) use engine::ResearchLoop;` so the moved struct stays reachable at `crate::research_loop::ResearchLoop`. (l) (#451): a `super::X` path INSIDE relocated code is DEPTH-SENSITIVE. Moving a fn from `commands/foo.rs` into a deeper child `commands/foo/render.rs` changes what `super` means — a `super::X` that resolved to the GRANDPARENT now points wrong; repoint to absolute `crate::commands::X`. grep `super::` BEFORE carving. The moved `mod tests`' own `use super::*;` is FINE (its super is the new owner module). serde_json `json!` macro IS carried into a child by `use super::*;` from a parent `use serde_json::json;`. (m) (#452): LEAN IMPORT DISTRIBUTION gives a clean first compile with ZERO unused-import warnings — facade imports ONLY what the facade BODY uses; each child gets its OWN explicit `use` for external crates + `crate::` helpers the facade does NOT import. A `crate::` helper the facade ALSO imports reaches children via super::*. It is SAFE for a child to ALSO explicitly import a name the facade has (explicit + glob coexist, explicit priority, no E0252, no unused). Cross-cutting PRIVATE helpers used by >=2 children but NOT the facade body live in the facade ROOT (seen by every child via super::*; a facade-private fn used only by descendants is NOT dead_code). (n) (#453/#458/#459): LEAN IMPORTS CAN STRIP A NAME THE TESTS RELIED ON. The original `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` saw every top-level `use` via its `use super::*;`. After a lean split the facade/owner imports ONLY what its body uses, so a type the tests reference but no production code in the SAME module (now the facade) does is NO LONGER in scope — SCAN the carved test body for names from the original import block and add explicit `use` lines for the missing ones (compile.rs: `use crate::provenance::ProvenanceGraph;`; pdf.rs: `use crate::WikiError; use std::path::Path;`; research_loop.rs #459: `use std::path::{Path, PathBuf}; use std::time::Duration; use crate::WikiError; use crate::research::{AcceptedNoteDraft, ResearchStopReason}; use crate::session::AcceptedResearchNote;` — the facade only does re-exports so it imports NONE of these). The moved tests' `use super::*;` still picks up pub(crate) items re-exported by the facade globs (e.g. parse_model_action via `pub(crate) use helpers::*`). (o) (#454) INTEGRATION-TEST CRATE SPLIT (tests/*.rs, NOT a src facade — NO pub(crate) widening at all): a file directly in `tests/` is its OWN test binary; Cargo ALSO AUTO-DISCOVERS `tests/<name>/main.rs` as a single test target named `<name>` (NO Cargo.toml `[[test]]` entry needed). Split `tests/cli_smoke.rs` -> `tests/cli_smoke/{main.rs,...}`: main.rs = facade (top imports + ALL shared helper fns + `mod child;` decls), each test-group child = `use super::*;` + its `#[test]` fns. CRITICAL: a `mod common;` referenced from the OLD top-level file resolves relative to the NEW file's dir once moved one level deeper — rewrite as `#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;`. (p) (#456) SPLITTING A FILE THAT IS ITSELF A DIR-SUBMODULE: import_resolution/parser.rs (1,045->6) is a submodule of import_resolution/ whose SIBLINGS (context/helpers/predicates, declared `pub(super)`) it imported via `super::context::{..}`. Splitting into parser/ puts children ONE LEVEL DEEPER, so a child's path to those siblings becomes `super::super::<sibling>` (the FACADE mod.rs stays at the SAME depth -> keeps `super::<sibling>` UNCHANGED). `pub(super)` siblings = visible to the WHOLE import_resolution subtree, so the deeper descendants reach them with NO sibling widening; `crate::models::X` (absolute) is depth-invariant. (q) (#457) A CHILD THAT ENDS UP WITH A `#[cfg(<platform>)]`-ONLY USE OF AN IMPORT trips `unused_imports` on the OTHER platform under -D warnings. GENERAL RULE: after a lean split, any name a child uses ONLY under a platform/feature cfg must itself be cfg-gated or fully-qualified, because the sibling that incidentally kept it live may have moved to a different child. (r) (#458) PUB-USE RE-EXPORT vs PUB-DEFINITION ASYMMETRY under cfg-gated/test-only consumers. rustc's dead_code lint is LENIENT on pub/pub(crate) DEFINITIONS (a pub fn/struct in a CRATE-REACHABLE module is exempt even if unused in the lib target) but unused_imports is STRICT on `pub use child::Name` RE-EXPORTS (warns under -D warnings if Name is not consumed within the crate's lib target). Two failure modes: (1) a GLOB `pub use child::*` survives if >=1 item is consumed (default passes via a cfg(documents) consumer) but FAILS --no-default-features when ALL consumers are gated out; (2) NAMED `pub use child::{A,B}` is checked per-name and fails even under default features for any name consumed ONLY by tests (cfg(test) is a SEPARATE target from lib). FIX: (a) declare child modules holding cross-feature/test-only pub items as `pub(crate) mod child;` so those pub items stay crate-REACHABLE and dead_code-exempt; (b) tests import via child paths `use super::child::{..}`; (c) re-export from the facade ONLY names actually pathed by EXTERNAL consumers, gated with the SAME cfg as those consumers. ALWAYS establish the no-default baseline on HEAD FIRST then validate BOTH default and no-default after the split. (s) (#459) SPLITTING A TYPES/DATA MODULE AWAY FROM ITS IMPL — A PRIVATE-FIELD STRUCT MUST CO-LOCATE WITH ITS IMPL (research_loop.rs 1,090->5: research_loop/ facade `pub(crate) use {engine::ResearchLoop, helpers::*, types::*}` / types(ResearchLoopConfig+Input+ModelRequest+ModelDecision+ResearchObservation+Event+Result+ResearchLoopDeps+ALL traits)+engine(ResearchLoop struct+its impl+private LoopState/StepOutcome/NoteWriteResult)+helpers(prompt render/action parse/source validation)+tests). The natural split puts public DATA types in types.rs and the engine impl in engine.rs. The central `ResearchLoop` struct has ALL-PRIVATE fields (root/config/model/ask/search/read/ingest/note_writer) that its `impl` reads on `self.*` — leaving the struct in types.rs while its impl moves to engine.rs trips 33x E0616 'private field' (a sibling module canNOT read another module's fully-private fields; gotcha (f) at scale, surfaced AFTER the first build not by static analysis). FIX (cleaner than widening every field): MOVE the private-field struct INTO the module that holds its impl (engine.rs) so impl+struct share a module and privates stay in-module; external consumers only use `ResearchLoop::new(..)`+methods (never field access), so re-export from the facade `pub(crate) use engine::ResearchLoop;` and they're unaffected (research/mod.rs imports it unchanged). KEY ASYMMETRY: a `pub` field inside a `pub(crate)` struct is ALREADY crate-visible (effective pub(crate)), so the sibling `ResearchLoopDeps` (all `pub` fields, an API param struct research/mod.rs builds via literal) + the config/input/ModelRequest/ModelDecision data types (all `pub` fields) STAY in types.rs with ZERO widening — only FULLY-PRIVATE-field structs trip E0616. When moving the struct: (a) REMOVE its name from the child's `use super::types::{..}` (now defined locally -> else E0255 'defined multiple times'); (b) ADD to that import every TYPE the struct's FIELDS name that the child did not already import — ResearchLoop's `&mut dyn ResearchModel/WikiAsk/WikiSearch/WikiRead/SourceIngestor/ResearchNoteWriter` fields forced adding those 6 trait names to engine's super::types import (they were types-internal before, now cross-module field types). An inherent `impl<'a> ResearchLoop<'a>` works in engine.rs as long as the type is in scope via `use` AND same crate. No cfg in this file (production unconditional) so both feature sets are identical; still validated both. (7) Validate (run feature variants if the file has `#[cfg(feature=...)]` branches; gcore default=[] so use `--features full`): `cargo clippy -p <pkg> --all-targets -- -D warnings` (single command compiles every crate + all test targets), `cargo fmt --all` then `--check` (use `textwrap.dedent` on a carved mod-tests body to avoid a leading-blank-line fmt diff; fmt then only re-wraps now-longer `pub(crate) fn` sigs), `cargo test -p <pkg> <module>::` to run just the moved tests (`--lib` to skip integration targets; for integration-test-crate splits use `--test <name>`; module path after split is `<mod>::<child>::tests::*` e.g. `db::resolution::tests`, `research_loop::tests`). RE-RUN clippy + tests AFTER the final `cargo fmt --all` so readiness evidence post-dates the last file edit (fmt is a file edit; task-transitions gate 1 clears earlier evidence). (8) Commit path-scoped: `git commit -m '...' -- <explicit paths>` (-m BEFORE --; include both the deleted original path and the new dir; git auto-detects renames, fine — shows as full delete + N new). WATCH the shared working tree: other sessions' uncommitted WIP must NOT be staged — `git add <my paths>` explicitly, verify `git diff --cached --stat` shows ONLY your files, never `git add -A`. Wiki audit unsupported-claim exemptions (crates/gwiki/src/audit/claims.rs + audit.rs). The line-granular claim model (`claim_lines`: one claim per physical line, credited only if that line carries an inline `[[knowledge/sources/...]]` / `[path:line]` span) over-flags flowing/generated prose. Layered exemptions:
1. `is_generated_code_projection_page` (path `code/` + frontmatter `trust: generated` + `generated_by: gcode-codewiki`) — page-level exempt; the codewiki projection identity IS the grounding. Covers code/files, code/modules, code/repo.md. (a94983985, #17703; dropped project-vault unsupported_claim_count 121451 -> 7.)
2. `DEFAULT_IGNORED_SECTIONS` (audit.rs) — sections whose bodies are source material, not synthesized claims: citations, sources, backlinks, extracts, `source excerpts` (added #17704), used by, missing evidence, conflicting claims.
3. `daemon_synthesis_attributed_sections` (#17704) — on AUTO-GENERATED daemon-synthesis concept pages ONLY (`source_kind: concept` AND frontmatter `synthesis_mode: daemon`), a section whose body carries an inline source attribution (e.g. a trailing `_Source: [[knowledge/sources/...]]_` line) credits ALL that section's wrapped prose claim lines. The daemon attributes each synthesized section to its sources at the section level, not per wrapped line.

BOUNDARY (refines the original 'knowledge/** stays fully audited'): CURATED knowledge (compile articles / research notes, NOT `synthesis_mode: daemon`) stays fully per-claim audited — that remains the right bar for human multi-source synthesis. Only DAEMON-GENERATED concept pages get generation-level (section/page) crediting, mirroring the code-projection exemption. Verified live 2026-07-07 with rebuilt gwiki 0.8.0: `gwiki audit --project d45545c5` unsupported_claims 7 -> 0 (was claude-concept.md/gemini-concept.md Overview prose + Source excerpts).

Standalone gcode/gcore currently has no encrypted secret store without the Python daemon. Gobby's close_task LLM validator compares the diff against the literal text of validation_criteria — not the spirit. When a reasoned mid-implementation decision diverges from the criteria (directory renames, path shifts, choice-of-approach changes), validation will fail even if the deviation was correct. The recovery path is: (1) update_task(task_id, validation_criteria=<rewritten to match reality>), then (2) close_task(task_id, commit_sha, changes_summary) — re-run normally, no skip.

Do NOT try skip_validation=true with commit_sha. Gobby explicitly blocks that combination with: 'Cannot skip validation when a commit_sha is provided. If you're linking a commit, you did real work — let validation verify it.' The block is intentional: real work must be verified against something rewritten, not bypassed.

Discovered on task #11793 (2026-04-15) when I committed `.upgrade/` after the criteria said `_upgrade/`. The switch was the correct call (dot-prefix dirs are auto-skipped by SkillLoader._load_skill_files at src/gobby/skills/loader.py:658; underscore dirs would have leaked into loaded_files as resources), but the validator couldn't tell from the diff alone.

How to apply going forward: any time a mid-implementation change diverges from the text you wrote at claim time, plan on update_task before close_task. Better still — write validation_criteria at creation time loosely enough that reasonable judgment calls don't require a rewrite: specify *what must be true when done*, not *which exact path or name to use*. If the divergence is too large to rewrite cleanly, escalate_task instead of fighting the validator.

Gobby task #15265 cut daemon code-index graph ownership over to gcode 0.9.2+: Python daemon no longer owns CodeGraph/Falkor read-write paths; /api/code-index/graph routes are HTTP shims over gcode graph commands, graph sync uses `gcode graph sync-file --project <root> --file <file>`, and clear uses `gcode graph clear --project-id <project_id>`. For gcode, `grep` is intentionally grep-shaped by default: when global `--format` is omitted, `gcode grep ...` uses text output. Use explicit `--format json` for the JSON envelope. Other gcode commands keep JSON as their omitted-format default.

For AGY/Grok provider planning: keep existing Gemini CLI support functional but mark it deprecated. Implement #15037 with Grok live integration via `grok agent stdio` and AGY as a visible provider stub/unavailable health state for live web chat/agent spawning until Antigravity CLI ships a documented machine transport such as ACP/stdio JSON-RPC or equivalent. In Gobby, terminal agent child sessions must be expired whenever their agent_run reaches a terminal status (`success`, `error`, `timeout`, or `cancelled`). `LocalAgentRunManager` owns immediate session expiry for terminal status transitions, and `AgentLifecycleMonitor.expire_terminal_run_sessions()` sweeps already-terminal runs so live tmux shells at prompts do not keep Sessions Live entries visible. Lifecycle timeout cleanup should mark agent runs as `timeout`, not generic `error`.

In gobby-cli, `.gobby/handoff-*.md` files are ignored by `.gitignore` via `.gobby/**`; they are local session handoff artifacts. Update them on disk when requested, but do not force-add/commit them unless the user explicitly asks for a tracked handoff artifact.

Gobby wiki health cron history (`gobby:wiki-health`) stores a compact user-visible summary from `src/gobby/wiki/scheduled_jobs.py`: known health list fields are represented as `<field>_count` plus the first 10 entries in `<field>_sample`, and `result.gwiki` keeps only `ok`, `command`, and `stderr`. Full detail remains in wiki health artifacts such as `meta/health/latest.json`.

Pipeline import/export gap: Pipeline definitions are DB-only at runtime (load_pipeline queries DB, not filesystem). The CLI `gobby pipelines import` command uses the Lobster parser which does NOT support native pipeline YAML format — it fails with 'PipelineStep requires at least one execution type' because it doesn't map the `exec` field correctly. sync_bundled_workflows runs at daemon startup but may not overwrite existing DB entries with updated YAML. There is currently no clean way to re-import a single updated pipeline YAML into the DB or export a DB pipeline back to YAML. This is a known gap that needs addressing.

During PostgreSQL Phase 7, SQLite runtime migrations are removed. `run_migrations()` only applies `tests/fixtures/sqlite_test_schema.sql` when `GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1` and `GOBBY_SQLITE_TEST_SCHEMA_PATH` are set; that protected fixture baseline initializes empty SQLite test DBs only and does not repair mutated runtime SQLite state or recreate removed FTS objects.

Gobby wiki broken-link convergence design: broken wikilinks in session digest pages (wiki/knowledge/sources/*.md) are NOT plain hygiene debt — they are gwiki upkeep's work queue. upkeep::run() re-derives entity clusters from lint's broken_links on every run (crates/gwiki/src/upkeep.rs), creating concept pages for targets with >= min_mentions (default 2, max 10 pages/run); singleton mentions stay as convergence signal until future digests re-mention them. Mass de-linking digests destroys this pipeline. Repair broken links only when they can never converge: links to purged/nonexistent knowledge/sources pages, bare version/round numbers, code-symbol refs, and generated surfaces (knowledge/INDEX.md is rebuilt by catalog::regenerate from the source manifest — fix the generator, never hand-edit; fixed in #17629 to link only digests that exist on disk). Librarian misclassification of pending-entity mentions tracked in #17640.

Gobby merge-orchestrator no-progress redispatch protection is intentionally scoped to the current orchestrator run: it should block a new merge-worker only after that run has waited for a worker and observed unchanged merge_status with pending conflicts. Historical task_delivery_campaigns.last_error / failed campaign reports are evidence for reporting, but must not by themselves prevent a fresh worker dispatch after automation fixes. Active inspect_merge_state resolutions with active_resolution_id should be continued before merge_abort is considered.

Gobby pre-commit verification: defined in .gobby/project.json under 'verification' and 'hooks'. Pre-commit runs 'lint' (uv run ruff check src/) and 'format' (uv run ruff format --check src/) on ALL of src/, not just staged files. Must pass before commits go through.

Gobby spawn_agent project-path resolution now happens in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_factory.py: explicit project_path wins, then current project context, then the resolved parent_session_id's project repo_path via LocalProjectManager. Gobby memory_dream supports unscoped wait=false by creating one aggregate background run with start_all_due_projects_async/execute_all_due_projects_run; route and MCP surfaces should return 202/started with that aggregate run_id instead of rejecting missing project_id.

Auth system architecture: Web UI auth uses Fernet encryption (SecretStore) for password storage, NOT PBKDF2 hashing. The password flows through ConfigStore.set_secret() like any other secret. is_secret_key_name() detects 'auth.password' because _SECRET_SUFFIXES includes bare 'password' (added in #9055). Auth routes do simple plaintext comparison against the Fernet-decrypted stored password. The CLI command is `gobby auth` (with --remove flag to disable). Frontend uses useAuth hook + LoginPage component with auth guard in App.tsx.

Neutral-cwd feature-LLM CLI compatibility matrix (src/gobby/ai/_text_generation_adapters.py). Per-CLI requirements (verified against vendor docs via context7 + live test): Codex `exec` aborts outside a Git repo ('Not inside a trusted directory and --skip-git-repo-check was not specified') — MUST pass `--skip-git-repo-check`. Qwen (gemini fork) degrades to 'restricted safe mode' for untrusted folders (ignores project settings/env/memory) — graceful, that IS the desired isolation, no flag needed. Droid `exec` has no git/trust gate and is already HOME/XDG-isolated, no flag. Claude (SDK) sets cwd explicitly and needs no git repo. RULE: when adding/modifying any feature-LLM CLI adapter, check its working-dir/trust gating against vendor docs before assuming the neutral cwd just works. # Review Lesson: Log temp cleanup failures after successful persistence

After a temporary media asset has been successfully copied or persisted to its final vault location, cleanup of the source temp file should be best-effort. A deletion failure at that point should log a warning and preserve the successful ingestion result, rather than replacing it with a cleanup error. Propagate cleanup errors only before the durable result exists or when cleanup is the primary operation being reported.

Evidence: task #478 updated `crates/gwiki/src/ingest/video/assets.rs` to warn on sampled temp-frame cleanup failures after frame persistence; validation passed with `cargo test -p gobby-wiki --no-default-features ingest::video`, `cargo test --no-default-features`, and `cargo clippy --no-default-features -- -D warnings`.

gobby-sessions:compact_self on a TERMINAL CLI session works by injecting the CLI's slash compaction command into the session's own tmux pane. In src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal.py: _CLI_COMPACT_COMMANDS maps source->command ({'claude':'/compact','codex':'/compact','gemini':'/compress','qwen':'/compress','droid':'/compress'}); compact_self resolves the command and calls _send_terminal_compaction_command, which FIRST sends _CODEX_INTERRUPT_KEY (an interrupt) to the pane, THEN sends the slash command literally.

GOTCHA: because the interrupt preempts the in-flight compact_self tool call itself (it runs in the caller's own session), the harness surfaces compact_self as 'The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use. The tool use was rejected.' immediately followed by the slash command (e.g. /compact) actually running. That 'rejected' message is NOT a user decline — it is compact_self working as designed (self-interrupt + slash-command injection). Do NOT treat a 'rejected' result after compact_self as the user declining; the compaction fired and succeeded. Confirmed by Josh in session #6992 (2026-06-09).

In macos.py GhosttySpawner.spawn(), if env vars are provided, they're converted to shell exports and prepended to the command: `exports = " ".join(f"export {k}={v};" for k, v in env.items())` then `shell_cmd = f"{exports} exec {shlex.join(command)}"` with `ghostty_args.extend(["-e", "sh", "-c", shell_cmd])`.

CSS code-splitting gotcha in Vite/React SPAs: When extracting CSS from a monolith index.css into component-scoped CSS files, beware that Vite code-splits CSS alongside lazy-loaded components. If Component A uses CSS classes that were extracted into Component B's CSS file, those styles won't load when only Component A is active.

Specific cases encountered during index.css decomposition:
1. `.conversation-picker` styles were in SessionsPage.css but used by ChatPage — moved to chat/styles.css
2. `.session-item`, `.session-group` shared primitives were in TerminalsPage.css but used across chat/sessions/terminals — moved to index.css (always loaded)
3. `.workflows-*` layout classes in WorkflowsPage.css used by SkillsPage.tsx — added WorkflowsPage.css import to SkillsPage.tsx
4. `task-execution.css` import was missing after Activity Panel tabs were refactored — fixed in commit 67024049
5. `files-code-viewer` and `files-tree-*` CSS rules were in FilesPage.css but needed by Chat UI file tree — extracted to chat/styles.css to decouple Chat UI styling from FilesPage.css and enable reuse of file tree styles across different contexts.

Rule of thumb: styles for classes used across multiple code-split boundaries must be in a globally-loaded CSS file (index.css or main.tsx import) or imported by all consuming components. When CSS breaks during component restructuring, check for missing stylesheet imports first.

Investigation: Expander Agent Replacing Task Decomposition (#8943)

## Key Finding: Expansion is Already Skill-Driven

The old expansion.py (TaskExpander) has been REMOVED. Current architecture:
1. Skill (expand/SKILL.md, 458 lines): Instructs AI agent to analyze codebase, generate spec, create subtasks
2. MCP Tools (_expansion.py): save_expansion_spec, execute_expansion, get_expansion_spec
3. Flow: Agent reads task -> analyzes codebase (Glob/Grep/Read, visible) -> generates spec -> saves -> executes atomically
4. Compaction recovery: save_expansion_spec persists spec to DB, get_expansion_spec detects pending for resume

## Assessment: Dedicated Agent Has Questionable Value

Current skill approach advantages:
- Conversation visible to user (transparency, debugging)
- Uses existing session context (codebase knowledge)
- No spawn latency
- Interactive (user can guide decomposition)
- Session compaction recovery via save/resume

Dedicated agent approach would add:
- Isolated context (won't pollute session) 
- Parallel execution capability
- But: loses interactivity, visibility, existing context, adds spawn latency

## Recommendation: Keep Skill-Based, Enhance with Rules

Rather than spawning a dedicated agent, add expansion quality rules:
- before_tool on save_expansion_spec: validate subtask count (warn if <2 or >15)
- Validate description length (warn if any subtask <50 chars)
- Validate TDD compliance (check code/config tasks have TDD headers)
- Validate dependency graph (warn on circular deps)

This gives enforcement benefits without dedicated agent complexity. The expansion is already agent-driven — the skill IS the agent behavior, just running in the current session.

Feasibility of dedicated agent: MODERATE technically, LOW value proposition.

Design token gotcha: --accent-foreground is the foreground color paired with bg=--accent (chartreuse). It is theme-flipping (near-black in dark, near-white in light). NEVER use it as a generic high-contrast text token. It only renders correctly when the background is also paired-flipping in the same direction (--accent, --color-error, --color-success-foreground, etc.). When the background is fixed-bright in both themes (e.g., PROVIDER_COLORS hex literals from sourceTheme.ts) or absent (inline SVG with currentColor), light-mode text becomes near-white-on-bright = invisible. Two real bugs found and fixed in commit 312cf65c8: (1) .source-icon-codex inline SVG, (2) .agent-def-badge--filled. Rule for review: any color: var(--accent-foreground) without a sibling background: var(--accent) (or var(--color-error|warning|success|*-foreground)) in the same rule is a contrast bug.

Session title native support: ClaudeTranscriptParser emits content_type='session_title' for Claude ai-title records, DroidTranscriptParser emits it for Droid session_start.sessionTitle, and ProcessorTranscriptMixin._extract_native_titles strips those metadata messages before rendering while updating the session title with title_source='native'. Digest title synthesis in gobby.memory.digest still allows title_source='native' to be replaced by title_source='llm'.

During #12761 PostgreSQL migration coordination, #14892 fixed a gobby build deadlock where merge-workers successfully merged worktrees but could not call record_merge_result because the task dispatch mutex was attached to the parent merge-orchestrator run. Commit 9dde6a5ca lets a direct merge-worker child release its parent merge-orchestrator mutex before recording the merge result, with regression coverage in tests/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/test_record_merge_result.py.

gobby-core keeps local backend data types/base URL helpers lightweight without HTTP dependencies. The HTTP probe APIs (`detect_backend`, `validate_backend`) and ureq-backed helpers are behind the `local-backend` feature. The `ai` feature includes `local-backend`, while `gobby-local`/gloc opts into `gobby-core/local-backend` without enabling the heavier `ai` feature.

In the gobby Rust workspace (crates/), gobby-core (crates/gcore) is a shared library crate, not a standalone CLI binary. Do not install or surface it in ~/.gobby/bin alongside gcode, ghook, or gwiki unless the workspace adds a real binary target.

In the gobby repo, the gobby-wiki MCP tool `wiki_trust` is a read-only wrapper over `GwikiGateway.trust()` / `gwiki trust --format json`; it should use `read_call` and must not pass through `WikiUpdateCoordinator` or other write-result handling.

In gobby-cli, `gobby-core` Qdrant unit tests live in `crates/gcore/src/qdrant/tests.rs`; `crates/gcore/src/qdrant.rs` declares `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` and keeps production Qdrant API/logic in place. Qdrant naming helpers remain in `crates/gcore/src/qdrant/naming.rs`.

Task #12250 changed `ChatterboxTurboProvider.warmup()` to prime the remaining cold synthesis path after model load and reference conditioning by running one throwaway capped generation (`_WARMUP_PRIME_TEXT='warm up'`, cap `min(config_cap, 8)`) under the normal synthesis lock. Task #12628 added TTS enable prewarm behavior: the web client includes STT/TTS intent in `voice_prepare`, server-side `voice_mode_toggle(enabled=true)` starts voice warmup, `voice_prepare` can arm TTS before the toggle frame arrives, and the web TTS button calls `prepareTTSPlayback()` in the click handler to unlock the browser AudioContext so the first spoken response is not muted. The UI renders/pulses warmup state while `voice_loading` is true.

HTTP MCP execution must seed SessionContext from the X-Gobby-Session-Id caller header before considering arguments.session_id. This prevents parent calls targeting agent sessions from inheriting the child's step workflow. Terminal agent cleanup should clear task_dispatch_mutex rows by run_id and workflow_instances by child_session_id. Regression coverage is defined in tests/servers/routes/mcp_endpoints/test_execution_session_end_cleanup.py and tests/mcp_proxy/transports/test_stdio_session_resolution.py.

In Gobby memory storage, the memories table currently has no normalized_content column; content normalization for duplicate-safe memory creation is implemented by stripping and storing the normalized text in the existing content column, with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by fetch/restore of hidden duplicates.

session_transcripts table was dropped in migration v150. Transcript storage is now filesystem-only via transcript_archive.py (~/.gobby/session_transcripts/). No more DB blob storage. BASELINE_VERSION was 150, now 151.

Task #17231 decomposed web/src/components/chat/styles/input.css into a 5-line public CSS import facade. The implementation now lives in input-base.css (legacy chat input, toolbar, scope, file preview, command palette, send/stop controls), input-voice.css (voice/PTT/listening indicators), input-composer.css (new composer shell, overlay, toolbar, model controls, agent status bar), input-responsive.css (status/voice controls plus media/container queries), and input-status.css (voice status bar). Tests that inspect input.css directly should resolve local @import rules first, as mobileChromeCss.test.ts, typographyLadder.test.ts, and planApprovalDesign.test.tsx now do.

One-shot LLM lane contract (daemon text generation, established task #17061, 2026-06-12): codex/gemini adapters in src/gobby/ai/text_generation.py enforce a no-tools one-shot contract matching the claude/haiku lane. Codex: start_thread(approval_policy="never", sandbox="readOnly") + ONE_SHOT_DIRECTIVE appended to system_prompt (rides in context_prefix). ACP lanes (gemini/grok/qwen): same directive + deny-all pre_tool_callback through ACPClient.send, so ACP permission requests answer {"outcome": "cancelled"} instead of the default auto-approve (managed web-chat sessions with pre_tool_callback=None keep auto-approve). Reasoning effort stays AUTO on codex one-shots — Josh's explicit call: the latency win comes from removing the agentic turn, not clamping reasoning. Per-candidate timeout: GenerationConfig.candidate_timeout_seconds (default 60s) wraps every candidate attempt in both text and JSON loops; on timeout the loop logs 'candidate timed out after Ns' and falls through to the next candidate. Why: feature_mid went gemini-primary in commit 126905f7f and every tasks.validation call burned 57-242s on an auto-approved agentic gemini turn then failed JSON parsing ('Expecting value: line 1 column 1'). Known residual: fresh codex app-server spawn per call costs ~6-8s (probe ~12s); warm-reuse of the daemon's pre-warmed client is task #17062. Big-prompt asks can still exceed the 60s cap on codex and fall back to claude — by design.

Pre-ship Gobby config should not add broad compatibility for removed file keys. For code-index summary config, keep nested symbol_summary as the accepted shape and reject flat summary_* fields; only drop daemon-owned internal cleanup keys when needed.

Gobby web UI cleanup direction: Project, Cron Jobs, Reports, and Traces should no longer be top-level hamburger/sidebar pages. Preserve Chat page functionality, including Activity panel cron/traces/reporting-style operational views where still used, and keep shared hooks/APIs that Chat depends on.

For Gobby 0.5.0 cleanup, tasks.assignee was removed completely. Task ownership now uses claimed_by_session_id with a real sessions FK plus task_stage_states for lifecycle/projection. Tests must seed real sessions before writing claimed_by_session_id; dangling owner ids are invalid. The legacy FalkorDB config key databases.falkordb.requirepass is rejected for new writes/imports and dropped when loading DB config stores so old local DB rows do not break daemon startup.

PipelinesTab dropdown bug fix: The '+ Pipeline' dropdown was rendering inside PipelinesTab's filter bar instead of inside the .workflows-new-wrapper div in WorkflowsPage. CSS expects position:absolute dropdown as child of position:relative wrapper. Fix: moved dropdown to WorkflowsPage, PipelinesTab now receives createMode prop ('builder'|'yaml'|null) and reacts via useEffect.

During PostgreSQL migration build coordination for #12761 on 2026-05-21, #14951 (per-session writable UV cache for spawned agents) and #14954 (reset lifecycle stage/claim/mutex after provider startup or spawn failure) were merged into 0.4.7, but the Gobby daemon was still running pre-restart code afterward (uptime 3h34m, PID 41596). A new #14954 QA worker still hit the uv cache permission path until it manually set UV_CACHE_DIR. Restart the daemon after the active #14119 worker reaches a safe point so future reviewer/merge spawns pick up the merged fixes.

MCP proxy tools work correctly when progressive discovery is followed: list_mcp_servers → list_tools → get_tool_schema → call_tool. The previous 'Invalid arguments: Unknown parameter' errors were caused by skipping get_tool_schema and guessing parameters. 10 stale memories reinforcing a CLI workaround were deleted on 2026-03-27. Always use progressive discovery, never skip to call_tool.

Gobby merge tooling fix #14886: merge_apply must distinguish active MERGE_HEAD finalization from direct/no-MERGE_HEAD completion. If MERGE_HEAD exists, resolved conflict rows can be written/staged/committed even when legacy resolution rows have source_branch/target_branch inverted; only verify the checkout is still on the worktree branch. Keep source_branch_validation_error for no-MERGE_HEAD direct completion. Commit f0cca8374 added regression coverage in tests/merge/test_merge_direct_git.py.

Spawned agents with inline step workflows may skip an initial `claim` step when spawn-time auto-claim has already assigned the task to the child session. `spawn_agent_impl` initializes those workflow instances at the task-claimed transition target with `task_claimed=true`, preserving ownership safety while avoiding redundant `claim_task` calls that can trap agents before review.

Phase 7 PostgreSQL-only runtime semantics: `gobby postgres uninstall` and the legacy `clear_postgres_fields()` helper must preserve a valid PostgreSQL runtime bootstrap (`hub_backend=postgres` plus `database_url` or `database_url_ref`) and reject attempts to restore `hub_backend=sqlite`.
