gobby-voice MCP tool registry created at src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/voice.py. Follows the config registry pattern (same deps: config, config_store, config_setter). Provides 4 tools: add_vocab, remove_vocab, list_vocab, clear_vocab for managing Whisper custom vocabulary. Wired in registries.py after the config registry block. Vocabulary persisted via ConfigStore.set('voice.whisper_vocabulary', terms). InternalToolRegistry.get_tool() returns the function directly (not an object with .handler), so tests should call tool(**kwargs) not tool.handler(**kwargs).

In Gobby, code-index navigation enforcement is normalized through src/gobby/hooks/code_navigation.py and src/gobby/hooks/normalization.py. Broad rg/grep/git grep/find and broad source reads get canonical_code_navigation_* metadata; successful gcode navigation sets code_index_navigation_used_this_turn so follow-up source line context can be allowed within the same turn.

Web chat sentence collision bug: In websocket/chat.py, all TextChunk events within a single request share one assistant_message_id. When the model outputs text → calls a tool → outputs more text, the ToolCallEvent handler flushes accumulated_text to DB and resets it, but the frontend keeps appending to the same message via the shared message_id. This causes sentence collisions like 'on?Ok'. Fix: track tool→text transitions with an `after_tool_call` flag, set it True on ToolResultEvent, and prepend '\n\n' to the first TextChunk after a tool call (guarded by checking accumulated_text doesn't already end with whitespace). The existing comment on line ~582 already described this exact class of bug for the DB persistence side but the frontend streaming side was missed.

When test fixtures create registries via create_workflows_registry(db=mock_db), the registry auto-creates WorkflowInstanceManager and SessionVariableManager from db. These managers call db.execute() and json.loads() on results, which fails with MagicMock. Fix: patch both constructors to return None so the registry uses backward-compat code paths that don't touch the db.

Gobby architecture convention: standalone step workflow definitions are no longer a supported public definition kind. Step workflows are owned inline by agent definitions via AgentDefinitionBody.steps / step_variables / exit_condition. Legacy workflow_type='workflow' rows may exist only for compatibility/migration paths and should not be planned as a new typed definition table.

In Gobby 0.4.0, task expansion is run-based: `gobby-tasks-ops:start_expansion_run` stores compile/apply/validation state on expansion runs; Plan-Coverage Contract plans compile deterministically through `src/gobby/tasks/expansion/_contract.py`; `apply_run` derives child stage manifests from the parent, attaches `expansion-run:<run_id>` provenance, and sets the parent `expansion_run_id` artifact.

As of task #14701, SessionLivenessMonitor treats a live recorded tmux pane as authoritative for tmux-backed terminal sessions. A dead stored terminal_context.parent_pid must not expire the session while the pane is still live; parent_pid only drives expiry for non-tmux rows or when tmux pane liveness cannot be verified. Tmux pane checks parse `#{pane_id}\t#{pane_dead}` and exclude pane_dead=1. The Sessions tab Live filter includes only active and paused; handoff_ready remains valid for handoff/proxy attach flows but is excluded from the Sessions tab Live list.

CronScheduler double-fire bug: next_run_at is only updated AFTER execution completes (scheduler.py lines 170, 181), but jobs dispatch as background asyncio.create_tasks (line 142). While a job runs, get_due_jobs() keeps returning it because next_run_at is still in the past. Fix: advance next_run_at at dispatch time before creating the background task. Timing: scheduler polls every 30s (config default), pipeline heartbeat is 60s interval, proposed conductor is 120s interval.

gobby-cli BM25 search score contract is centralized in gobby_core::search: BM25_SCORE_FUNCTION is `pdb.score`, BM25_SCORE_REGPROCEDURE is `pdb.score(anyelement)`, and bm25_score_expr(row_id) renders `pdb.score(<row id>)`. gobby-code and gobby-wiki should keep domain SQL builders in their own crates and consume these shared score primitives rather than inline score function names.

gobby-cli D5 gwiki research implementation commit f9bbde3 removes `gwiki research` daemon agent dispatch and CLI flags `--task-id`, `--agent-count`, `--resume`; `research` now accepts `--audit`, budget flags, `--ai`, and `--require-ai`, emits the D5 JSON shape (`query`, `audit`, `stop_reason`, `findings`, `gaps`, `warnings`, `changed_paths`), and deterministic `--audit --ai off` loads the checkpoint, clears stale daemon dispatch fields, and reports orphaned raw research notes without calling `/api/agents/spawn`.

SQLite migrations are flattened at baseline version 260. `src/gobby/storage/migrations.py` has `BASELINE_VERSION = 260`, `_MIN_MIGRATION_VERSION = 260`, and an empty `MIGRATIONS` list; historical SQLite upgrade support below v260 is intentionally unsupported/reset-required. Fresh databases rely on `baseline_schema.sql`, which includes the folded v259/v260 objects: `idx_ism_completion_lookup`, `idx_chat_attachments_local_path`, `trg_chat_attachments_bound_at_write_once`, and `trg_chat_attachments_updated_at_touch`.

In gobby-cli tasks #802/#803, `gcode prune` behavior changed: unscoped `gcode prune` still prunes stale indexed projects globally, then re-collects remaining indexed projects and runs best-effort FalkorDB graph and Qdrant vector orphan cleanup for each project using `Context::resolve_for_project_id_with_services(..., ServiceConfigSelection::projection_cleanup())`. Scoped `gcode --project <path-or-name> prune` keeps projection orphan cleanup limited to the resolved project. The pre-release `Context::resolve_for_project_id()` wrapper was removed in #803; project-id-only callers must use `resolve_for_project_id_with_services` and state their service needs explicitly, e.g. `ServiceConfigSelection::falkordb_only()` for `graph clear --project-id`.

MagicMock(spec=WorkflowDefinition) does NOT auto-expose Pydantic v2 model fields. When testing code that accesses fields like `.enabled`, `.sources`, etc., you must explicitly set them on the mock (e.g., `wf.enabled = True`). This is because Pydantic BaseModel fields aren't visible as class-level attributes to Mock's spec introspection.

Task #15320 Gobby-side spawn env work is partially complete in commit a42dbfb52: SpawnRequest/SpawnResult moved to spawn_models, spawn_cache_policy centralizes UV_CACHE_DIR/CARGO_HOME/PATH handling, and spawned tmux agents now explicitly receive ~/.gobby/bin in PATH plus sandbox write access for managed tool/cache paths. Live qa-reviewer worktree e2e proved PATH was fixed, but pre-spawn gcode indexing still timed out after 120s because current gcode treats isolated worktrees as fresh full project indexes. Remaining blocker is gobby-cli support for parent-baseline plus worktree-overlay indexing before #15320 can close.

For the Gobby 0.5.0 AI capability registry boundary epic, prefer clean capability-binding cutovers and do not add backward compatibility shims or transitional aliases for old/abandoned provider config surfaces.

Gobby hub storage is PostgreSQL-only. The PostgreSQL adapter currently accepts legacy hub placeholders (`?` and `$N`) and remaps them to psycopg `%s` at execution time; this is a compatibility layer for existing storage call sites, not SQLite support. Any new or changed SQL must still be PostgreSQL-compatible, and direct `%s` usage may be preferred where a local module has already migrated to psycopg-native placeholders.

Gobby docs roadmap context as of 2026-05-24: SQLite and Neo4j migrations are complete. PostgreSQL is the runtime hub baseline and FalkorDB is the graph baseline. Roadmap target sequence: 0.5.0 is the new post-data-migration baseline release; 0.5.0+ focuses on UI hardening and Rust port work; 0.6.0 is the Rust port release; 0.6.0+ starts Gobby Pro remote sync across multiple Gobby-controlled machines; 0.7.0+ is the Gobby Pro beta with fleet management and a shared dashboard; later work prepares 1.0.0 with SWE-bench benchmarks.

web UI code surfaces: react-syntax-highlighter (Prism, useInlineStyles=true) writes the theme's `pre[class*="language-"]` background as an INLINE style on the PreTag element (highlight.js: `Object.assign({}, defaultPreStyle, customStyle)`). In practice passing `customStyle.background:'transparent'` does NOT reliably override the rendered inline `background: var(--code-bg)`. To make a CodeBlock/JsonBlock/DiffBlock render transparently (sit on the surrounding surface instead of its own --code-bg slab) you must add a scoped CSS class with a `!important` rule. The established convention (added for #14721) is the `.tool-code-surface` class on the chat tool-result CodeBlock/JsonBlock/DiffBlock/MarkdownBody instances, with this rule in web/src/components/chat/styles.css: `.tool-code-surface > div, .tool-code-surface > pre, .tool-code-surface [class*="language-"], .tool-code-surface :is(div,pre):has(> code[class*="language-"]) { background: transparent !important }`. The `:has()` arm catches react-syntax-highlighter's class-less PreTag div when nested (e.g. MarkdownBody fences). buildCodeBlockTheme stays the source of truth for the theme-aware syntax palette + textShadow:none; file viewers (FilesTab/FileChangesTab) intentionally do NOT carry the class so they keep a distinct code surface. Reuse `.tool-code-surface` for any future 'code block should blend with its container' need rather than fighting customStyle.

In gobby-cli, gwiki URL ingest is organized with crates/gwiki/src/ingest/url.rs as the public orchestration/data-type module and child modules under crates/gwiki/src/ingest/url/: fetch.rs for HTTP fetching, redirect/SSRF/body-limit validation, render.rs for URL markdown rendering and HTML text extraction, and tests.rs for URL ingest unit tests. Savings reporting should use daemon/API-backed reporting rather than direct SQLite writes. Older gcode notes about direct SQLite savings writes are stale after the PostgreSQL hub cutover; gcode is built from crates/gcode in the gobby monorepo and should integrate through current hub/API behavior.

Gobby PostgreSQL storage migrations are flattened for the 0.5.0 baseline through migration 305 (2026-07-02, commit 93ab56e77): `BASELINE_VERSION` is 305, `postgres_baseline_schema.sql` contains the final schema/seed state through 305 (native uuid identity columns everywhere, including unmodeled_observation_events.session_id / unmodeled_observations.example_session_id with UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT dedup), and `src/gobby/storage/migrations/` has no SQL migration files. Fresh installs record schema version 305 after applying the baseline and `latest_known_version()` == 305. Future schema changes use new file-based SQL migrations numbered above 305; the authoring rules (dual-shape validity against both populated pre-migration schemas and the fresh baseline, preflight DO guards for data-dependent uuid casts, NULLIF '' sentinel pattern) live in the migrations.py module docstring and are enforced by tests/storage/test_migration_contract.py (test_uuid_cast_migrations_ship_a_preflight_guard binds all future files). Hubs below 305 take the corrupt_partial backup/recreate path. The baseline remains a CURRENT full-schema snapshot: on fresh installs any on-disk migrations replay on top of it, so migration files and baseline must stay in sync.

LocalDatabase.connection is a @property (not a method/context manager). Use db.execute(sql, params) directly for queries, or db.transaction()/db.transaction_immediate() as context managers for writes. Don't use 'with db.connection() as conn:' — it will fail silently.

In gobby-cli CI, env-gated gcode graph_standalone coverage is provided by .github/workflows/ci.yml job `gcode-graph-standalone`: it uses a FalkorDB service container with password `gobbyfalkor`, builds `gobby-postgres-ci:18-pgsearch` from `crates/gcore/assets/postgres-pgsearch` with pg_search 0.23.4/SHA 6b042d61d156ca5fdcb1c417e291d90bffe3026848890be30bf6e578146b4676, runs `gcode setup --standalone --no-services`, then runs `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p gobby-code --no-default-features --test graph_standalone` with GCODE_GRAPH_STANDALONE_* env vars so the suite executes instead of skipping.
Gobby is fully on PostgreSQL for hub storage. New storage SQL should use PostgreSQL/psycopg bind placeholders directly and should not rely on a storage-layer qmark placeholder remap.

Gobby stack architecture uses PostgreSQL for concurrent/team/hosted storage, FalkorDB for Cypher-style graph storage (over task dependencies, memory links, plan coverage, code-symbol references, and agent spawn trees), and Qdrant for vector storage. The migration of the daemon/runtime architecture to Rust is active.

Cron-triggered pipelines have no session by default. spawn_agent requires parent_session_id, so CronExecutor._execute_pipeline must create a session via pipeline_executor.session_manager before calling execute(). Without this, dispatch_batch silently fails with success:false. Fixed in commit 09a87a80.

In gobby-cli/gwiki/gcode after daemon routing validation #694, operative text generation routing is `ai.text_generate.routing: auto` with provider/model unset so clients use daemon profile `feature_low` and resolve to frontier providers such as Codex/Claude. LM Studio embeddings are unaffected. Heavyweight codewiki aggregate docs (module/repo/architecture) should move to a mid profile — task #696.

Prefer localized fixes that match existing patterns unless the user explicitly asks for broader redesign.

RuleEngine implementation (task #8806): The core RuleEngine is in src/gobby/workflows/rule_engine.py. Five effect types: block (with tool/mcp/command matching), set_variable (with expression evaluation via SafeExpressionEvaluator.evaluate_value()), inject_context (template accumulation), mcp_call (records in metadata), and observe (appends structured entries to _observations in variables dict). gobby-cli operational gotcha: `cargo nextest run -p gobby-code` intermittently STALLS at the multi-binary `--list` enumeration phase in the shared working tree (concurrent agent sessions + chrome-devtools-mcp saturating disk I/O). Symptom: compile shows 'Finished test profile' but no 'Starting N tests'/PASS lines; every test binary (incl. unrelated ones like contract, vector_projection, gcode) sits at 0% CPU STAT S for minutes. It is ENVIRONMENTAL, not a code bug (the same tree passes on retry; unrelated binaries hang identically). How to handle: (1) for fast focused validation run `cargo test -p gobby-code --lib <module>` (single lib binary, no fan-out, ~1s warm); (2) to get the clean full nextest the close validator requires, just RETRY — it completes once contention clears (verified 923 passed on retry); (3) do NOT kill the nextest parent to unstick it (the wrapping shell then skips to the next command, e.g. NEXTEST_EXIT=143); diagnose via `pgrep -P <nextest_pid>` looking for `deps/*--list` children at 0% CPU.

Diagnosing an opaque 'Gobby pre-commit verification failed' git commit failure: the .git/hooks/pre-commit hook runs `gobby hooks run pre-commit 2>/dev/null`, which spawns a FRESH `gobby` CLI that imports the whole gobby package. Any import/syntax error anywhere in src/gobby (including unrelated, uncommitted working-tree edits from another session) makes that import fail and blocks EVERY git commit in the repo — even commits that don't touch the broken file. The hook swallows stderr, so the message is opaque. To see the real cause, run `gobby hooks run pre-commit` directly (un-redirected). The already-running daemon is unaffected (it holds the old code in memory), so MCP/daemon calls keep working while local commits are blocked. Workaround for an unrelated commit: `git commit --no-verify` after validating your own diff independently; do not edit the other session's in-flight broken file.

Graph search works by: (1) vector search on _Entity nodes to find similar entities, (2) follow MENTIONED_IN links to get direct memory IDs, (3) graph traversal via find_related_memory_ids for related memories. CLI workspace trust mechanisms for agent spawning:

- Claude Code: Trust stored via ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/ directories. Path encoding replaces / with -. Creating this directory pre-approves the workspace. --dangerously-skip-permissions only bypasses tool permissions, NOT workspace trust.

- Gemini CLI: Projects tracked in ~/.gemini/projects.json. --approval-mode yolo only bypasses tool approval, NOT workspace trust.

Memory search ranking invariant (SearchService._build_results, src/gobby/memory/services/search.py): final results are sorted SEMANTIC-FIRST always — key (similarity is not None, similarity, ranking_score) — regardless of rrf_applied. Vector similarity is the quality signal; RRF/graph/keyword lists only EXPAND recall and break ties, they must never displace a high-similarity hit from top-K. Do NOT 'fix' this to make ranking_score (RRF) primary: that was tried in #17102 (commit 7b29cb5fd) and reverted in #17105 (commit e0dd0e980) because graph_search defaults to True (persistence.py:120) and rrf_applied is True for ANY >=2-source query, so RRF-primary went live for nearly all searches and regressed recall (e2e graph_off recall@5 0.573 vs RRF-primary 0.320). RESOLVED in #17104 (commit bf04ee74c): the way useful graph traversal lift reaches results without displacing strong semantic hits is NOT RRF-primary — it is a synthetic ENTITY-COSINE similarity for graph-only hits, placed on the same cosine axis (ranking_mode 'graph_synthetic', discount 0.9), so the larger cosine always wins and semantic-first is preserved. #17104 also fixed a FalkorDB cosine-distance vs similarity bug in vector_search that was the real reason graph signal never reached results. See [[e4ff3445]] (full #17104 design) and memory 98415ca7 (the #17102 gate numbers).

## Skill Injection Architecture Decision (In Progress)

The skill auto-injection pipeline is currently broken end-to-end:
- `discovery` skill has `alwaysApply: true` but is never injected at session start
- `inject-skills-on-start` rule is `enabled: false` and its template `{{ skills_list }}` references a variable the rule engine never populates
- `SkillInjector.select_skills()` is fully implemented but never called in the session-start path
- `_db_skill_to_parsed()` doesn't reconstruct `audience_config` from DB, so 15+ audience-scoped skills lose their config
- `_inject_context_aware_skills()` is an intentional stub returning empty string
- `canvas` skill's `conditions:` frontmatter is dead data — parser ignores it

**Proposed direction (Josh thinking on it)**: Instead of `alwaysApply` on skills, make the default agent always apply to web sessions. The agent becomes the composition unit that bundles the right skills for its context. "Always-apply the agent, not the skill." Users could create custom web chat agents with different prompts/skills. This eliminates the need for a skill injection path that works outside agent scope.

**Key insight**: `discovery` skill not injecting may explain why agents struggle with MCP progressive disclosure.

**Open question**: Chicken-and-egg — need to wire up the default agent as the web UI agent that always starts on web chats. If that's done, no need for agent-less skill injection path.

Gobby MCP Progressive Disclosure: The flow is STRICT and hook-enforced: list_mcp_servers() → list_tools(server) → get_tool_schema(server, tool) → call_tool(server, tool, args). Each step gates the next. The gobby MCP system exposes 15 proxy tools (including add_mcp_server, call_tool, get_tool_alternatives, get_tool_schema, get_variable, import_mcp_server, list_mcp_resources, read_mcp_resource, remove_mcp_server, and others). These proxy tools are top-level deferred tools (e.g. mcp__gobby__get_tool_schema). ToolSearch does NOT return these proxy tools — they must be called directly or discovered via introspection. Never skip list_tools — the hook will block get_tool_schema if you haven't called it for that server. NOT all 15 tools are directly accessible as top-level proxy tools in Claude Code: add_mcp_server, remove_mcp_server, and call_tool work as direct proxies, but at least 3 (status, get_tool_alternatives, and one other) are not directly accessible. Full accessibility mapping requires systematic testing.

Gobby secrets storage now uses envelope encryption: each secret value is encrypted with a random Fernet DEK stored in `secret_key_material`; the DEK is wrapped by a KEK. File decomposition patterns used to bring 4 files under 1,000 lines:

1. **Package extraction** (spawn_agent.py 1016→5 files, max 540): Convert single file to package with __init__.py re-exports. Best when file has 4+ distinct responsibility groups. Follow existing pattern (tasks/ was already a package).

2. **Module-level function extraction** (runner.py 1068→807 + 2 modules): Extract groups of standalone methods into separate modules as functions. Used runner_broadcasting.py (160 lines) and runner_maintenance.py (120 lines). Works when methods are self-contained utilities called during init.

3. **Mixin extraction** (chat.py 1153→774 + session_control.py 439): Extract methods into a new mixin class, add to WebSocket server's inheritance chain. Follow existing mixin pattern (HandlerMixin, AuthMixin, etc.). Use TYPE_CHECKING for cross-mixin method references.

4. **Helper deduplication + setup extraction** (install.py 1114→942 + install_setup.py 119): Extract repeated output formatting into helper functions (_echo_install_details, _echo_uninstall_details). Move setup logic to separate module. Use re-export for backward compatibility with test patches: `_ensure_daemon_config = ensure_daemon_config`.

Key lesson: When moving functions that are patched in tests, either (a) keep the call site in the original module so patches still work, or (b) update all test patch targets. Option (a) is safer when there are many patches.

Gobby daemon text-generation debugging gotchas (verified 2026-06-10): (1) ai.text_generation._log_generation_event lines in gobby.log only appear at INFO for FAILED candidate calls — successful generations are silent there, so absence of feature_llm_call lines does NOT mean no calls happened; check gobby-error.log and page output instead. Corollary: a clean gobby-error.log during a generation window while the CLIENT records failures means the daemon returned 'success' with bad content — check for empty text, prompt echo, or client-side citation stripping. That exact pattern exposed codex/gpt-5.3-codex-spark echoing the full prompt as a successful response (gobby#15816, found 2026-06-10; feature_mid's primary candidate, so bare feature_mid one-shot calls return garbage-as-success until fixed). A2UI Canvas architecture: Components are defined in a flat surface map keyed by unique IDs (not nested). Parent components reference children via `children: { explicitList: ["child-id"] }`. Data binding uses BoundValue objects: `{ literalString: "text" }` for literals, `{ path: "field/name" }` for data model binding. The render pipeline is: A2UIRenderer -> RenderComponent -> Component -> RenderChildren (for containers) -> RenderComponent (recursive). Container components (Row, Column, Card, List) must pass both `updateField` and `depth` props through to RenderChildren, otherwise nested form inputs silently break. Backend canvas.py uses in-memory state (_canvases dict) with canvas_present copying HTML files to get_gobby_home()/canvas/. Files at web/src/components/canvas/ (frontend) and src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/canvas.py (backend).

Pipeline condition bug: Jinja2 renders boolean `false` as the string "False" which is truthy. Pipeline conditions like `${{ steps.X.output.completed if steps.X.output else false }}` always pass because the else branch renders "False" (non-empty string). Fix: use `${{ steps.X.output.completed if steps.X.output and steps.X.output.completed else '' }}` to ensure empty string on failure.

Embedding provider policy in Gobby: runtime embedding calls use the configured embeddings.model/api_base/api_key/dim only. In gobby-code, `.h` language detection is intentionally signal-based: sibling `.m`/`.mm` or Obj-C directives (`@interface`, `@protocol`, `@import`) route a header to `objc`; C++ keywords such as `class`, `namespace`, or `template` route to `cpp`; otherwise `.h` defaults to `c`. This keeps C/C++ headers eligible for the clangd semantic resolver while avoiding static first-match Obj-C capture.

When sessions crash during workflow engine refactoring, new sessions often pick up the same work and commit under new task IDs, leaving original tasks stale in in_progress state. To triage: cross-reference git log task ID tags against open task list, run the actual tests mentioned in bug tasks to check if issues still reproduce, then close as already_implemented (with commit_sha from the actual fix commit) or duplicate. close_task with reason='already_implemented' or 'duplicate' auto-skips validation but still needs commit_sha if the original session had edits.

In gobby-cli, gwiki synthesis is split with `crates/gwiki/src/synthesis.rs` as the public facade. Child modules live under `crates/gwiki/src/synthesis/`: `types.rs` defines `ArticleKind`, synthesis input/source/prompt/page types, and write outcome/policy types; `generate.rs` contains article/source-page synthesis orchestration and explainer grounding; `paths.rs` contains vault-boundary checks, slug/link/relative-path helpers, and source-page path/link selection; `render.rs` contains frontmatter, source excerpt, list-section, and YAML scalar rendering helpers; `write.rs` contains write policy checks and atomic page writes; `tests.rs` holds the existing synthesis behavior tests with narrow imports for private helper coverage. The facade still exports the public synthesis/write APIs and data types.

In the gobby task storage package, task lifecycle event storage lives in src/gobby/storage/tasks/_lifecycle_events.py. TaskLifecycleEventManager returns TaskLifecycleEvent objects and lists in insertion order by default for audit assertions; the module-level record_lifecycle_event helper returns the inserted event id, and module-level list_lifecycle_events returns newest-first using created_at DESC, id DESC to satisfy the #12784 task API.

In gobby-cli gwiki session ingest, secret redaction must sanitize both the rendered session Markdown and the `SourceManifest` metadata (`location`, `citation`, `title`). `index_after_ingest` can index manifest-backed text, so redacting only message bodies or final Markdown can still leak raw `/Users/<user>` paths, emails, or API-key-like tokens into downstream indexed document/chunk text. Implemented for #812 in `crates/gwiki/src/ingest/session.rs` and `crates/gwiki/src/ingest/session/redaction.rs` with commit dca3914.

Gobby's memory IndexingService coalesces concurrent global embedding reindex requests with a service-level in-flight task, so duplicate callers await the same rebuild result instead of logging a post-rebuild unchanged-snapshot skip. Sequential same-snapshot global calls still dedupe for 60 seconds by fingerprinting the source memory snapshot and verifying Qdrant point IDs match, preserving manual repair reindexes after the short window and invalidating the dedupe cache when vector indices are cleared.
